title: isLastToolInvocationFollowedByText() should ignore text parts that originate from the same model response as the tool call
body:
### Description

### 📄 Description  
`gemini-2.0-flash-001` sometimes generates function calls with a **leading text part that is just a newline character (`\n`)**.  

This causes an issue in `useChat()` where **tool call results are not submitted automatically**, and the conversation gets stuck. The user then has to manually continue the conversation to submit the tool call result.

I have configured `useChat()` with `maxSteps` set to 10 and `streamText()` in the backend with `maxSteps` set to 1 (default). This means that the client will handle the resubmit.

---

### ⚠️ Problem  
Sometimes (not always), Gemini responds in the following format:

```json
{
  "id": "msg-llkj9PNWMkILH5gkJRFMjlu3",
  "createdAt": "2025-03-19T17:22:50.373",
  "role": "assistant",
  "content": "\n",
  "parts": [
    {
      "type": "tool-invocation",
      "toolInvocation": {
        "state": "result",
        "step": 0,
        "toolCallId": "ezv9IDtNtQrqvptU",
        "toolName": "updateState",
        "args": {
          "op": "replace",
          "path": "/basic/document_name/fi",
          "value": "Testing testing"
        },
        "result": "State updated."
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "\n"
    }
  ],
  "toolInvocations": [...],
  "revisionId": "ogxXwFFQmJomF6lT"
}
```

After this message is streamed and handled by the `useChat()` hook, **it does not get submitted back to the model for the next step**, because [shouldResubmitMessages()](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/46c85b5a1e08ee0887c9fe9f27da6db6a8db12f7/packages/ui-utils/src/should-resubmit-messages.ts#L4) returns `false`.

The reason is that [isLastToolInvocationFollowedByText()](https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/46c85b5a1e08ee0887c9fe9f27da6db6a8db12f7/packages/ui-utils/src/should-resubmit-messages.ts#L34) returns `true` due to the trailing text part `"\n"` – even though it was created **before** the tool call result.

---

### 💡 Suggested Fix  
A potential fix would be to **ignore trailing text parts that are empty or just whitespace/newlines** inside `isLastToolInvocationFollowedByText()` logic.

Alternatively, a more robust solution would be to **ignore text parts that originated from the model's tool call message** as those texts does not mean that the model has answered to the results yet.

---

### ✅ Expected Behavior  
If a tool invocation result is followed only by a text part that was created in the same model response as the tool call itself, tool call results should be automatically submitted back to the model.

---

### 🙏 Request  
Please consider improving `isLastToolInvocationFollowedByText()` to either:

- Ignore text parts that are just whitespace, or  
- Ignore text parts that were part of the model's original tool call message

### Code example

_No response_

### AI provider

@ai-sdk/google 1.1.12

### Additional context

_No response_

linked_prs.title: fix (ui): introduce step start parts
linked_prs.body:
Fixes #5276 

## Background

#5276 showed that LLMs might produce text after a tool calls, leading resubmit not working. Introducing step start parts will solve this and provide additional benefits:

- can be rendered if desired
- will enable removing `step` number of tool invocation parts eventually
- provides part that step information can be attached to

## Tasks

- [x] implementation
   - [x] create step start part type
   - [x] update and test `get-message-parts`
   - [x] add step start parts when processing stream
   - [x] test `should-resubmit-messages`
   - [x] update `append-to-response-messages` to save step start parts
   - [x] add ui test cases specific to empty text after tool invocation
- [x] examples
   - [x] update tool call ui example
   - [x] update single message persistence ui example to render step start parts (and reload)
- [x] docs
   - [x] update useChat reference
   - [x] add to chatbot with tools guide
- [x] changeset

ai_judgment.response:
Yes.

This is an agent issue because it involves handling LLM provider responses (Gemini), tool invocation logic, and agent workflow (automatic resubmission of tool call results). The problem and suggested fix are specific to agent system behaviors and orchestration between LLM output and tool handling.
